articles.title: The Law of the Locker Room #ufc
articles.description: There's an unwritten code in the fight game, and Chael Sonnen is explaining how it works. Chael describes something known as a "receipt." When you do something to another person and they eventually return the favor, the score is settled. In the locker room, the expectation is simple: if you know you deserved it, you accept your receipt, let it go, and move on. But there's another side to that code. According to Chael, the rules of the playground are different. If somebody does something to you and you never respond, people may look at you differently. Chael makes it clear that he didn't create these rules, and he doesn't necessarily agree with them. He's simply explaining the culture and unwritten expectations that exist inside combat sports. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #FightCulture #MMAStories

articles.title: Amanda vs. Kayla BOMBED—Now What?
articles.description: Amanda Nunes vs. Kayla Harrison had everything a major fight should have: a world title, a GOAT debate, history between the fighters, and two separate promotional campaigns. According to Chael Sonnen, the audience still didn't care. Now the UFC has a much bigger problem. Despite the lack of interest in their first fight, Chael can't identify another opponent for Amanda or Kayla that fans would rather see. So what do you do? Run back a fight that already failed to capture the audience—or make an even less interesting matchup in hopes of building something for the future?

articles.title: How the UFC Can Set Up Hokit vs. Pereira #ufc
articles.description: How does the UFC make Josh Hokit vs. Alex Pereira happen? Chael Sonnen believes the answer starts with Alexander Volkov. There are several ways the matchup could come together. If Pereira loses, he could potentially be matched with Hokit. If Pereira wins but doesn't receive the next title shot, that could also open the door. But Chael sees an even better route: give Volkov a shot at the heavyweight championship. That move could help clear the path for Hokit and Pereira to meet, regardless of the outcome of Pereira's fight with Sergei Pavlovich. Chael explains why Volkov getting the title opportunity may be the key to making one of the most exciting heavyweight matchups possible. #UFC #JoshHokit #AlexPereira #AlexanderVolkov #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Israel Adesanya’s Interview Has Me VERY Concerned
articles.description: Israel Adesanya says he stopped using his greatest weapon, his fight IQ, and is now getting back to being “The Stylebender.” Chael Sonnen isn't convinced that's the answer. Chael explains why fighters are often the last people to recognize their own decline, why changing gyms and searching for new answers concerns him, and why no amount of mindset or fight IQ can replace the physical work required to return to the top. Chael remains an Adesanya fan and hopes he's proven wrong. But after hearing Izzy explain his path back, he calls it the most concerning Adesanya interview he's ever seen.

articles.title: Here's How We Get Hokit vs. Pereira
articles.description: Josh Hokit and Alex Pereira have made it clear they want to fight each other. Chael Sonnen believes there's a path to making it happen, and Alexander Volkov may hold the key. Chael breaks down the moving pieces at heavyweight, including Tom Aspinall's absence, Ciryl Gane's next title defense, Pereira's fight with Sergei Pavlovich, and Volkov's increasingly public campaign for a title shot. If Volkov can get Hokit and Pereira occupied with each other, Chael believes his own path to Gane opens up. And Hokit vs. Pereira could become the “people's main event” on the same card.

articles.title: Joe Rogan Is Wrong About Ilia Topuria
articles.description: Joe Rogan believes Ilia Topuria should return to 145 pounds after facing Justin Gaethje at lightweight. Chael Sonnen strongly disagrees. Chael argues that Topuria and Gaethje both weighed exactly 155 pounds, and rejects the idea that Gaethje was simply “too big” for Ilia. He also believes their fight was much closer than people remember and questions why a world champion would cut weight to avoid tougher competition. From Topuria and Gaethje to Jon Jones, Alex Pereira and Josh Hokit, Chael explains why he believes the entire conversation about who is “too big” is fundamentally flawed.

articles.title: Harrison vs Nunes 2 at 145? Nunes Says "Rematch Accepted"
articles.description: Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes in the fourth round at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. Two days later, Nunes posted "145 Rematch, accepted." Dana White's answer: "Sure. Yeah. I'd do it again." We trace both careers through the MMA Weekly archive: Nunes's run from UFC 200 to the double-champ night against Cris Cyborg, the Peña loss, the rematch and her 2023 retirement; Harrison's two Olympic golds, two PFL titles and her UFC run through Holm, Vieira and Peña. Then the round-by-round numbers from UFC 334, what a rematch at 145 would mean for a division with no champion since 2023, and what the 135 rankings look like if the champ moves up. Should Harrison vs Nunes 2 happen at 145? articles.title: Dana White Turns Down Press Secretary, Then Gives $500K at the White House
articles.description: In less than two weeks, UFC CEO Dana White went from a White House job offer to a half-million-dollar gift on the South Lawn. On November 7, President Trump announced on Truth Social that Dana White had been offered the job of White House press secretary. The next night in Palm Beach, Trump said he was "only kidding" but that "Dana loves the idea." On November 9, Dana stepped up to the briefing room podium, took questions from the press, and turned the job down: "I do not want to be in politics." On November 20, Trump and White hosted a reception honoring the U.S. Marine Band, "The President's Own," on the new White House helipad. The gift started at $200,000. Trump raised it to $500,000 and wrote the new number on the check by hand. White thanked the band for the live music at UFC Freedom 250, and the band celebrated its first-ever Grammy nomination. articles.title: Is Tom Aspinall's Comeback Worth the Risk?
articles.description: Tom Aspinall has a pivotal eye test coming in January, and Chael Sonnen has questions about what happens if he's cleared to return. A rematch with Ciryl Gane may seem like the obvious next step, but Chael questions whether coming straight back into a five-round fight against one of the world's best heavyweights is worth the risk. Gane has remained active while Aspinall has been recovering, and Tom has never gone five rounds in a fight. More importantly, Chael wants to know what it means that Aspinall's eye still requires a pivotal test before he can return—and whether there comes a point when the risk outweighs the reward.

articles.title: Hokit vs. Jon Jones? I've Got My Answer
articles.description: Chael Sonnen answers fan questions on another edition of Ask Uncle Chael, including one of the biggest heavyweight debates: who would win between Josh Hokit and Jon Jones? Chael makes his pick—and reveals that Hokit and Jones have actually trained together. He explains what he knows about Jones' training camp, why those private rounds matter, and what both men may already know about a potential matchup. Plus, Chael discusses reality TV, who should play him in a movie, Matt Lindland, Anderson Silva's barbecue invitation, his loss to Anderson, and why conditioning matters more than almost anything else in fighting.

articles.title: Ciryl Gane's Wins Keep Adding to Jon Jones' Legacy #ufc
articles.description: Every time Ciryl Gane wins, it adds another chapter to the Jon Jones heavyweight legacy debate. Chael Sonnen points out that nobody can deny how dominant Jon Jones was during the opening four minutes of their fight. Whether you're a supporter or a critic of Jones, that performance remains part of the conversation whenever Gane competes. But Josh Hokit has his own legacy to build. If he captures the heavyweight championship, he wants to make sure there's no question about the legitimacy of his reign. The goal isn't just to win the belt—it's to become an undisputed champion and separate himself from the debate surrounding previous heavyweight titleholders. Chael examines the connection between Gane, Jones, and the next generation of heavyweight contenders. #JonJones #CirylGane #JoshHokit #UFC #Heavyweight #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Should the UFC Sign Usman Nurmagomedov?
articles.description: Should the UFC sign Usman Nurmagomedov after what happened with Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi? Chael Sonnen looks at whether Usman's involvement should affect his future with the UFC or another major promotion. Merab says he has forgiven him, Usman has already faced serious consequences, and the incident unexpectedly helped turn Saba into a name people now want to see compete. Chael argues that acknowledging Usman's actions were wrong doesn't necessarily mean a promotion needs to punish him again, and he explains why the right response to someone who's already been punished is sometimes to help him back up.

articles.title: Did Josh Hokit Get Punished for Being Tough? #ufc
articles.description: Did Josh Hokit get punished for being tough? Chael Sonnen questions why Josh wasn't given the same opportunity for recovery after an accidental eye poke that a fighter would receive following a low blow. He points to Joe Rogan's discussion of the incident and argues that the rules shouldn't depend on how much punishment a fighter is willing to endure. Chael also compares the situation to Tom Aspinall's fight with Ciryl Gane, where an eye poke prevented Aspinall from continuing and a rematch was subsequently discussed. If an accidental foul makes one fighter unable to continue, why should the outcome be different simply because another fighter fights through it? Chael explains why he believes Hokit has a legitimate argument for a rematch—and why toughness shouldn't end up working against a fighter. #UFC #JoshHokit #CirylGane #TomAspinall #MMA #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Amanda Should NOT Fight Kayla at 145 lbs
articles.description: Amanda Nunes wants another shot at Kayla Harrison, this time at 145 pounds. Chael Sonnen explains why that might be the last thing Amanda should want. Chael believes Nunes looked extremely good in their first fight and understands why a rematch makes sense. There may not be a more interesting opponent available for either woman. But moving the fight to 145 changes the equation. Kayla's weight cut to 135 forces her to compete depleted. Give an Olympic gold medalist another 10 pounds to work with, and Chael believes Amanda would be facing a considerably more dangerous version of Kayla Harrison.

articles.title: Jake Paul Has a Problem
articles.description: Jake Paul believes bringing Khabib Nurmagomedov back for one fight could help change the fight business. Chael Sonnen isn't convinced. After Jake asked Khabib what it would take to compete again—including floating a hypothetical $200 million figure—Chael explains why everyone trying to lure Khabib back has focused on the wrong thing. According to Chael, money wasn't the biggest issue behind Khabib walking away. But Chael's bigger problem is Jake's belief that signing one massive star, or simply treating fighters better, can fundamentally change the industry. From the IFL to PFL and MVP, Chael looks at why the "fighter-first" approach hasn't translated into audience demand and questions what Khabib could actually change.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Deserves More Respect #ufc
articles.description: Josh Hokit may have lost to Ciryl Gane, but Chael Sonnen believes there's a lot more to take away from that fight than the result. Hokit was the undersized heavyweight, facing the very size and strength advantage that many believed would make Gane such a difficult matchup. He took the shots, battled through the pressure, got lifted off the canvas, and still gave Gane a tremendous fight. Chael believes Josh deserves enormous credit for his competitive spirit and performance. But he also has a message for Hokit fans: supporting Josh doesn't mean tearing down Ciryl Gane. Gane won a hard-fought fight, and both men deserve recognition. Chael explains why there's plenty to celebrate on both sides and why an immediate rematch isn't necessarily the answer. #JoshHokit #CirylGane #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews

articles.title: Bruce Buffer is Wrong
articles.description: Chael Sonnen explains why the viral moment between Josh Hokit and Bruce Buffer wasn't nearly as serious as some are making it out to be. According to Chael, Buffer took a small shot at Hokit first. Hokit responded with a middle finger, an equal and opposite reaction known in the locker room as a "receipt." At that point, they were square. The problem, according to Chael, is what happened afterward. He explains the unwritten locker room code, why Hokit's response was appropriate, and why Buffer should have simply let the issue end there.

articles.title: UFC 334 Scorecard Chaos: How Kevin Holland vs Uros Medic Became a Draw
articles.description: What really happened with the Kevin Holland vs Uros Medic scorecards at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. Bruce Buffer read the cards as 30-27, 29-28, 28-28 for a majority draw. The official scores were 28-28 (Michael Bell), 28-28 (Chris Lee) and 29-27 Medic (David Bruce). Medic lost a point in round two for low blows, and the deduction counted on all three cards. The difference was round one: Bell and Lee gave it to Holland, Bruce gave it to Medic despite Holland's knockdown.
